protocol.name: v5 integer-sample timing protocol
protocol.locked_at: Conditions were frozen before the full run, according to the source note; it is not described as a formal preregistration.
protocol.description: Pass requires maximum absolute component error <= 0.25. The protocol uses 2,000 noisy frames per vector and timing offset; the Wilson interval is conditional on the fixed vector panel and synthetic IID noise model.

baselines: oracle_exact_timing (diagnostic upper bound; not a competing decoder)

metrics.name: frame pass share
metrics.note: Two-sided 95% Wilson interval, conditional on the fixed vectors and synthetic IID draws.

metrics.name: frame pass share
metrics.note: Two-sided 95% Wilson interval, conditional on the fixed vectors and synthetic IID draws.

interpretation: In this synthetic software condition only, the existing nominal decoder passed 0 of 12,000 frames at +8 samples, while an oracle given the exact timing passed 11,346. The oracle is a diagnostic upper bound, not a timing-recovery algorithm or a fair competing decoder. This does not establish physical timing or device performance.
limitations: The vectors, waveform, timing offsets, and noise are synthetic and dimensionless; there is no physical channel or device measurement.
The chosen +8-sample offset is an arbitrary stress value, not a physical operating range.
The protocol is exploratory, not a formal preregistration or physical validation.
The uncertainty interval quantifies IID simulation variation conditional on the fixed panel and stated model, not model or physical uncertainty.
The oracle uses exact timing and is a diagnostic upper bound, not a timing-recovery method.
